prompt:
Write a police officer's crash report narrative (about 150 words). Collision type: rear-end collision in Pasadena, Texas. The claimant was a driver and reported neck strain. Refer to people as Driver 1, Driver 2 or Passenger. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1128; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury is plausible for a crash like this one.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- The damage does not match the story: the dents are on another side and at another height than the described impact.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
On the afternoon of the reported collision in Pasadena, Texas, Driver 1 was stopped in traffic when the rear of the vehicle was struck by Driver 2. Driver 2 said the impact happened as Driver 1 slowed. Driver 1 reported neck strain and said stiffness began within the hour. A rear impact of this kind can produce that injury, and nothing I observed made the reported symptoms unlikely.

Witnesses at the scene described the collision the same way Driver 2 did, and photographs taken on scene show the vehicles in the positions the parties gave. Driver 1 was in the vehicle at the time, as confirmed by Passenger and by a witness who saw Driver 1 in the driver's seat. I found no earlier damage to the vehicle, and Driver 1 is named on the policy covering it.

The damage to Driver 1's vehicle does not match the account given. The dents are on a different side from the impact described and sit at a noticeably different height. I photographed and measured the damage and referred the discrepancy for further review.
